idea: Investor relations support for Asian companies listing in London
buyer: Asian companies listing or listed in London
pain: They cannot communicate with Western investors effectively
v1: An IR programme for one listed Asian company
channel: Asia contacts plus London broker network
verdict: Genuine bilingual advantage and recurring fees, but London listings by Asian issuers are scarce.

why.distribution: Asian issuers in London are a small, cold population she would reach through brokers.
why.demand: Listed companies do pay IR retainers.
why.fmf: Language plus genuine understanding of what Western investors want to hear.
why.revenue_structure: Monthly retainers that renew for years.
why.defensibility: Bilingual IR with real buy-side credibility is scarce.
why.tailwind: Adverse - London listings are declining and Asian issuers are choosing other venues.
why.ceiling: £5k/mo x 4 clients = £240k, but there are few such issuers and fewer still that will buy.

ceiling_arithmetic: £5k/mo x 4 retained clients = £240k. Only four clients needed, but the addressable population of Asian issuers in London willing to pay is perhaps 20-30 and shrinking. Realistic: 1 = £60k.
carries: Only four clients to clear the target, with genuinely recurring retainers.
kills: A shrinking addressable market. London is losing listings, especially Asian ones.
test: Ask two London brokers how many Asian issuers they have and whether any lack IR support.
test_fail: They say the pipeline has dried up.
